archetype.name: Game Manager (short-area backup)
archetype.definition: A low-aDOT backup who lives on quick, on-schedule completions underneath and is fine in relief, but who hasn't shown he can create enough downfield or in the red zone to carry an offense over a full start.

report.headline: Competent underneath, reckless in the intermediate window: a backup who can't carry a start.
report.take:
Tyson Bagent is Chicago's QB2, and his 2026 is three appearances on 70 dropbacks: a short relief stint against Minnesota, a full game against the Jets (credited to Case Keenum as the starter, but Bagent played every offensive snap), and one true start at Green Bay that went badly. Caleb Williams has started every game since, so this is a spot-duty profile. The question is whether he can keep an offense functional when called on, not whether he's a starter.

The tape splits cleanly by depth. Inside 10 air yards he's good: a 78% completion rate, a CPOE of +5.5 and positive EPA, with short throws (0-9 yards) at +0.23 a play and a 62% success rate. That is the job Ben Johnson's offense asks of a backup, and the Jets game (+7.9 EPA on 34 attempts against a defense now ranked 25th) was that version of him. Past 10 yards it falls apart. On intermediate throws he completes 41.2%, sits nearly 14 points under expected, and has thrown all three of his interceptions. His aggressiveness has roughly doubled from 2023 (25.45% of throws into tight windows versus 12.6), and those tight-window throws into the 10-19 range are where the turnovers come from.

The raw numbers hide how uneven this is. His season EPA per dropback (-0.077, 35th of 49) blends one solid relief game with a disastrous start: -0.448 a dropback at Green Bay, a 23.8% bad-throw rate and two picks. The target split tells the same story. Rome Odunze turned 12 targets into +7.0 EPA, while Colston Loveland's 14 targets cost -8.2, almost all of it on the over-the-middle, intermediate work where Bagent's interceptions live. The 40% pressure-to-sack rate looks alarming, but it comes from a handful of pressured dropbacks, and in 2023 he ranked 4th of 66 at avoiding sacks under pressure. That one is mostly noise.

The 2023 baseline confirms the type. He was below zero in EPA then too (-0.093, 47th of 66), with a 6.01 YPA and a similar time to throw and aDOT. The short-game efficiency is real and repeatable. Zero touchdowns on 64 attempts and a 4.7% interception rate are partly small-sample extremes, but they point the same direction as his career: a serviceable relief arm, not someone who wins a game on his own.

strengths.title: Efficient on short, on-schedule throws
strengths.body: Inside 10 air yards he's accurate and keeps the offense on schedule, with completion rates well above expected and a 62% success rate on 0-9 yard throws. It comes from quick decisions in a structured, timing-based passing game. That kind of accuracy has held across his career, so it should last.

strengths.title: Can run the offense in relief
strengths.body: Against the Jets he played every snap and finished +7.9 EPA with a 5.6% pressure rate, the version of him the Bears want if Williams misses time. He works best against weaker defenses with clean pockets. A strong opponent exposes him far more.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance historically strong
strengths.body: His 2026 pressure-to-sack rate looks ugly, but it rests on very few pressured dropbacks. In 2023 he ranked among the best in the league at getting rid of the ball under pressure. His overall sack rate is still better than the league average, which fits the career version.

concerns.title: Intermediate throws produce the turnovers
concerns.body: All three interceptions came on 10-19 yard throws, where he completes 41.2% and sits nearly 14 points under expected. His aggressiveness has jumped from 2023, and these are tight-window throws he isn't hitting. That is a real flaw, not a role artifact: the throws he's choosing to force are the ones he misses.

concerns.title: Only start was a collapse
concerns.body: At Green Bay he was 12 of 21 for 87 yards with two picks and a -0.448 EPA per dropback, missing badly on nearly a quarter of his throws. One game is a small sample. Still, it matches a 2023 line that was also below average, so expecting a drop-off whenever he starts is reasonable.

concerns.title: No scoring punch
concerns.body: Zero touchdowns on 64 attempts and a -0.339 EPA in the red zone, where he completes under half his throws. Some of that is small-sample bad luck. But his short, low-aDOT style compresses badly near the goal line, so expect a low touchdown rate even after it normalizes.

trend.note: He went from a brief relief stint against Minnesota to a +7.9 EPA game against the Jets, then -10.3 at Green Bay, and hasn't taken a meaningful snap since Williams returned in Week 6. There's no trajectory to read, just a wide range of outcomes that depends heavily on the opponent.

nextGame.headline: Clipboard duty unless Williams goes down; Saints secondary is inviting.
nextGame.body:
Bagent is the QB2 and Caleb Williams, who has started every game since Week 6, isn't on the injury report here, so the base case is that Bagent doesn't throw a pass against New Orleans. If he were pressed into action, the matchup is about as soft as they come. The Saints rank 24th in defensive EPA and 22nd against the pass, allow 274.6 passing yards a game (29th), and are last in the league on deep throws. Their 22nd-ranked short-pass defense also suits his quick, underneath game. The one real threat is their 7th-ranked sack rate.

Availability on his side matters more than on theirs. Left tackle Braxton Jones is out for the season, and Luther Burden III, one of his two most-targeted receivers, is questionable with a concussion. That would leave Odunze, his most productive target, as the main read. On the Saints side, center Erik McCoy's biceps injury and the backfield injuries affect their offense, not the defense he'd face. The Bears come off a bye with 14 days of rest, and there's no line or weather yet.

keyMatchups.title: Short game against a soft underneath defense
keyMatchups.body: His best area, throws inside 10 yards, meets a defense that ranks 22nd on short passes. If he played, this is where he'd move the chains. It's the most bankable part of his profile.

keyMatchups.title: Saints pass rush vs. depleted line
keyMatchups.body: New Orleans gets home at the 7th-best sack rate, and Chicago is without Jones at tackle for the year. Bagent historically gets the ball out under pressure, but a quick rush would cut off the deep shots this defense gives up.

keyMatchups.title: Odunze against a leaky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Odunze has been his most efficient target, and the Saints let WR1s beat their usual output by more than three PPR points (28th) while ranking last on deep balls. If Burden sits, more targets go to Odunze.

nextGame.watch: Any change to Caleb Williams' status during the practice week. That alone decides whether Bagent plays.

restOfSeason.body:
As long as Williams is healthy, Bagent is a backup with near-zero weekly production; the projections below are what to expect per start if he's called on. The sustainable piece is the short-area accuracy, which held in 2023 and again this year. Expect completion percentage in the mid-60s and a safe, quick-game offense. The zero-touchdown line will regress upward with volume. His interception rate should also come down from 4.7%, but not to league average, given how often he's forcing intermediate throws.

Opponent quality is the biggest driver. He handled the 25th-ranked Jets and was overwhelmed by Green Bay, so a spot start against a weak pass defense could look respectable while a good one could get ugly. Without Jones at tackle, and possibly Burden, any starts would come with less help than he had in September. A realistic start looks like 150-230 passing yards, roughly one touchdown or fewer, and close to an interception.

projections.stat: Passing yards per start (if called on)

swingFactors: Whether he stops forcing intermediate throws
Opponent pass-defense quality if he starts

confidence.note: 70 dropbacks across three uneven appearances; he's currently a backup.
